title: Former exco members withdraw challenge against Negeri Sembilan govt, secretary over expulsion
text:
Former exco members withdraw challenge against Negeri Sembilan govt, secretary over expulsion Wednesday 18 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Highlight Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 18): Ten former Negeri Sembilan executive councillors on Wednesday withdrew their legal challenge to the validity of their expulsion from the state government.
 Their lead counsel, Datuk Mohd Hafarizam Harun, told Seremban High Court judge Roz Mawar Rozain that his clients had agreed to withdraw the action in both the High Court and the Federal Court, without liberty to file afresh.
 With the settlement, the 10 former exco members have also withdrawn their High Court challenge and the three sets of questions they had posed to the Federal Court. 
 The questions concerned the validity of their Sept 20 removal, which they said was done without the advice of Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim.
 The Federal Court had scheduled the matter for Dec 16.
 Hafarizam cited Ismail’s resignation as the menteri besar as the reason for withdrawing the challenge, arguing that when the MB resigns, "the entire exco falls".
 However, Roz Mawar pointed out that the resignation is in dispute and asked whether the Yang di-Pertuan Besar, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, had accepted it.
 It was reported that the Negeri Sembilan Palace had yet to verify the resignation of Juasseh assemblyman Ismail as the menteri besar, despite Barisan Nasional announcing it on Monday night.
 Hafarizam, who appeared with Syed Faisal Al-Edros Syed Abdullah and Mohd Amin Osman, said that while waiting for the royal decree on Ismail's resignation, the withdrawal needs to proceed. "That is the stand taken."
 Datuk Dr Cyrus Das, the lead counsel for Negeri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim who appeared with Abdul Rashid Ismail, said they accepted the withdrawal without liberty to file afresh but do not recognise the reason mentioned.
 “The withdrawal without liberty to file afresh should also include not filing the case via a judicial review,” he said.
 Razlan Hadri Zulkifli, who appeared with Marisa Regina Aris Rizal, concurred with Das on the withdrawal along with the lead counsel for the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU), Steven Thiru.
 The withdrawal came two days after parties indicated the possibility of a settlement to the case, which added to the present Negeri Sembilan imbroglio.
 The removal of the 10 exco members — Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah — was gazetted on Sept 24.
 Former exco members to pay costs as judge highlights time and resources spent
 Hafarizam said that following the withdrawal, the 10 former exco members were prepared to pay costs to Zafir, the Negeri Sembilan government and DKU.
 He offered RM20,000 each to Zafir and the state government, and RM8,000 to DKU.
 Cyrus, Razlan and Thiru, who appeared alongside David Mathew and Shafrin Halim, agreed to the arrangement.
 However, Cyrus reiterated that they did not recognise the reason given for the withdrawal of the 10 former exco members' legal action.
 Roz Mawar recorded the withdrawal of the originating summons without liberty to file afresh.
 The judge also said that the court did not discourage litigants from exercising their right to withdraw legal proceedings, noting that doing so might be the more prudent course of action.
 “Nothing said here is a criticism of the decision itself. But in the five months since this originating summons was filed with a certificate of urgency, much time and resources have been spent determining applications to intervene, giving directions for the stay application and dealing with other matters.
 “This court makes these observations not to censure anyone, but because the court’s jurisdiction is a public resource held in trust for everyone who comes before it. A party who invokes it, particularly as a matter of urgency and on constitutional questions concerning the government of the state, takes on a matching responsibility,” Roz Mawar said.
 She added that, as all the defendants had consented, the court struck out the originating summons without liberty to file afresh, with costs to be awarded as agreed.
 Also present at the proceedings were the Negeri Sembilan state legal adviser, Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal, and Tan Sri Azhar Azizan Harun, who appeared for two of the 10 former exco members from Perikatan Nasional.
